http.label: HTTP
http.title: The request arrives
http.text: Only signed-in people can book. The session is an opaque cookie, checked before the handler runs.

contract.label: Contract
contract.title: One schema, both ends
contract.text: The browser and the server agree on what a booking looks like: one Zod schema validates this body on the server and types the form in the browser.

idempotency.label: Idempotency
idempotency.title: Retries do not book twice
idempotency.text: If the phone sends the same booking twice, the second one gets the first answer back. The key and a hash of the body are stored; a repeat returns the stored response instead of running again.

repository.label: Repository
repository.title: Translate the database
repository.text: When the court is taken, the database says no and the app turns that into a clear answer: PostgreSQL refuses the insert with 23P01, which becomes a 409, the court is taken.

postgres.label: PostgreSQL
postgres.title: The database decides
postgres.text: The rule lives in the database itself: no two confirmed bookings for the same court may overlap in time. Whatever route inserts tomorrow, it still holds.

integration.title: Bookings in, invoices out
integration.headline: Event bookings in, invoices an accountant accepts out
integration.text: A mapping and normalisation layer between an events platform and an invoicing ERP: simplified invoices, management expenses and VAT. I learned the accounting domain from scratch to model it correctly.

standards.title: A standard the linter enforces
standards.headline: A code standard nobody has to remember
standards.text: There were no conventions. I wrote a layered architecture as lint rules, with size limits per layer, complexity limits and no any, plus the branching strategy, CI, Husky, Commitlint and pre-merge checks. I wrote it when we were two developers, and it held as the team grew.

product.title: A multi-tenant events platform
product.headline: One platform, every company its own
product.text: Role-based permissions, theming per company and department, itineraries, budgets and cost modules driven by formulas. Shipped to production.

cloud.title: Travel management on Azure
cloud.headline: A travel app, modelled from zero on Azure
cloud.text: An application for an external client. I designed its NoSQL data model from scratch on Cosmos DB, with files in Azure Storage.

game.empty: No response yet. Your request is one of 50 for {court} at {time}.
game.lose: You arrived {rank} of 50. Someone got the court first.
game.win: You arrived first of 50. The court is yours.
game.replayLose: Same key, same 201, served from the idempotency store. The winner still has one booking, not two.
game.replayWin: Same key, same 201. Still one booking: the retry was answered from the idempotency store.
game.lesson: That is the part that matters: a retry never books twice.
game.esNote: My API answers in Spanish: “that slot is already booked”.
game.keyHint: One key per booking attempt, so the server can recognise a retry.
game.utcNote: Times travel in UTC: {utc} is {time} in Madrid.
game.step2Win: Suppose that 201 never reached your phone: the connection dropped on the way back. Your app retries with the same key.
game.step2Lose: Now take the winner. Suppose its 201 never reached the phone: the connection dropped on the way back. Its app retries with the same key.
game.newKeyWin: A new key looks like a new booking. The court is already taken, by your own booking, so your phone is told it failed when it worked.
game.newKeyLose: A new key looks like a new booking. The court is already taken, by the winner’s own booking, so the winner’s phone is told it failed when it worked.
game.afterNew: Now retry with the original key.

race.label: Strategy

lock.label: Wait in line
lock.explain: SELECT … FOR UPDATE locks the court: the others wait their turn, then find the slot taken.

retry.label: Retry on conflict
retry.explain: Nobody waits: the losers see the version changed and try again, up to three times.

refuse.label: Let PostgreSQL refuse
refuse.explain: The EXCLUDE constraint rejects every overlapping insert with 23P01: the database decides.
